survey.title: Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotics: A Review Towards Real-World Applications
survey.abstract: Amid growing efforts to leverage advances in large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) for robotics, Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently gained significant attention. By unifying vision, language, and action data at scale, VLA models aim to learn policies that generalise across diverse tasks, objects, embodiments, and environments. This survey offers a comprehensive, full-stack review, integrating both software and hardware components of VLA systems, covering architectures, modality-specific processing, learning paradigms, robot platforms, datasets, and evaluation benchmarks.

rt1.title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale
rt1.highlight: First large-scale transformer model trained on 130k real-world robotic episodes, demonstrating strong generalization to unseen objects and tasks.
rt1.contribution: Proposed a transformer architecture that directly maps vision and language to robot actions at 3Hz. Trained on 130k episodes across 700+ tasks. Showed that scaling model size and data improves generalization to new objects, backgrounds, and tasks. Used a discretized action representation for stable training.

ablationStudy.finding: Scaling from 35M to 93M parameters significantly improves generalization
Training on diverse tasks is more important than task-specific fine-tuning
No pretraining needed; training from scratch on robot data suffices

rt2.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
rt2.highlight: Co-trained a VLA model on web-scale vision-language data and robotic data, enabling emergent capabilities like reasoning about object categories and symbols.
rt2.contribution: Co-trained a PaLI-X vision-language model on both web data and robot action data. Actions were represented as text tokens, allowing direct use of pre-trained VLM weights. Demonstrated emergent capabilities: reasoning about object categories, understanding symbols, and multi-step semantic reasoning.

ablationStudy.finding: Mixing robot and web data at 1:1 ratio yields best generalization
Discretizing actions into 256 text tokens enables stable co-training
Larger VLM backbone (5B vs 55B) shows clear scaling benefits for reasoning

cliport.title: CLIPort: What and Where Pathways for Robotic Manipulation
cliport.highlight: Combined CLIP for semantic understanding with Transporter Networks for spatial precision, enabling language-conditioned manipulation with 2D affordance maps.
cliport.contribution: Proposed a two-stream architecture: 'what' stream (CLIP) for semantic understanding and 'where' stream (Transporter) for spatial action prediction. Used language-conditioned attention over CLIP features to ground actions. Demonstrated one-shot imitation learning for tabletop manipulation tasks.

ablationStudy.finding: CLIP pretraining provides significant semantic grounding advantage
Separating what/where streams improves both precision and generalization

vlm-robot.title: Vision-Language Models as Robotic Affordance Providers
vlm-robot.highlight: Survey reference on how pretrained VLMs (CLIP, BLIP, etc.) provide semantic affordance and grounding for robotic perception and planning.
vlm-robot.contribution: Discussed how pretrained VLMs can serve as semantic understanding modules for robotics, providing open-vocabulary object recognition, affordance prediction, and task grounding without task-specific training.

openvla.title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model
openvla.highlight: A fully open-source 7B VLA model trained on Open X-Embodiment dataset, supporting multiple robot embodiments and showing strong fine-tuning capabilities.
openvla.contribution: Released a fully open-source VLA model (7B parameters) trained on the Open X-Embodiment dataset. Used a Llama 2 language backbone with a DinoV2 vision encoder. Supports multiple robot embodiments out of the box. Demonstrated strong fine-tuning performance on downstream tasks with minimal data.

ablationStudy.finding: DinoV2 outperforms CLIP for action prediction on robot data
As little as 100 demonstrations sufficient for strong task-specific performance

octo.title: Octo: An Open-Source Generalist Robot Policy
octo.highlight: A transformer-based generalist policy trained on 800k trajectories from Open X-Embodiment, supporting multiple observation and action spaces with flexible task conditioning.
octo.contribution: Proposed a transformer-based generalist policy with flexible observation and action space handling. Used readout tokens for task conditioning and action prediction. Trained on 800k trajectories from OXE. Supports natural language and goal image conditioning.

ablationStudy.finding: Handling variable camera counts improves real-world deployment
Language + goal image combination outperforms either alone

pi0.title: π_0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
pi0.highlight: A 3B parameter flow-based VLA model using a PaliGemma vision-language backbone with a flow-matching action decoder, trained on diverse multi-embodiment data.
pi0.contribution: Proposed a flow-matching based action decoder for continuous robot control. Used a pretrained PaliGemma VLM as the backbone. Trained on diverse data from multiple robot platforms. Achieved strong performance on complex multi-step manipulation tasks.

ablationStudy.finding: Flow matching provides more stable training for action generation
Pretrained PaliGemma provides strong visual-language grounding

pi05.title: π_{0.5}: a Steerable Generalist Robotic Foundation Model
pi05.highlight: Predecessor to π_{0.7}, introducing steerable context conditioning for diverse task execution strategies.
pi05.contribution: Introduced the steerable conditioning framework that allows the model to adapt its execution strategy based on multimodal prompts including subgoal images and task metadata.

diffusion-policy.title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion
diffusion-policy.highlight: Reformulated behavior cloning as a conditional diffusion model, enabling multimodal action distributions and state-of-the-art performance on manipulation tasks.
diffusion-policy.contribution: Proposed representing robot policies as conditional diffusion models over actions. Enabled capturing multimodal action distributions (important when multiple solutions exist). Achieved SOTA on 15/16 benchmark tasks. Introduced receding horizon control for closed-loop execution.

ablationStudy.finding: Diffusion outperforms GMM-based IBC on all multimodal tasks
2-step history sufficient; longer horizons hurt due to overfitting
Receding horizon control critical for robust execution

vit-robot.title: Vision Transformer for Robotic Perception
vit-robot.highlight: Survey reference on how Vision Transformers (ViT, DinoV2, SAM) serve as visual encoders in VLA models.
vit-robot.contribution: Overview of vision encoder choices in VLA: pretrained ViTs provide strong visual features; DinoV2 offers dense spatial features beneficial for manipulation; SAM provides object segmentation for affordance reasoning.

r3m.title: R3M: A Universal Visual Representation for Robot Manipulation
r3m.highlight: A visual representation pretrained on human video (Ego4D) that transfers zero-shot to robotic manipulation tasks.
r3m.contribution: Pretrained a ResNet50 on Ego4D human videos using a time-contrastive objective. Showed that human-centric visual representations transfer zero-shot to robot manipulation. Outperformed ImageNet pretraining on 12/13 manipulation tasks.

ablationStudy.finding: Human video pretraining outperforms ImageNet for manipulation
ResNet50 sufficient; ViT shows similar trends but requires more data

llm-robot.title: LLM as Robot Task Planner and Reasoner
llm-robot.highlight: Survey reference on how LLMs (Llama, GPT, T5) are used as language encoders and task planners in VLA systems.
llm-robot.contribution: Overview of language encoder choices: LLaMA for open-source VLA, GPT-4 for high-level planning, T5 for lightweight text conditioning. LLMs provide task decomposition, common-sense reasoning, and natural language grounding.

act.title: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
act.highlight: Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT): Predicts action sequences rather than single steps, enabling coherent multi-step execution.
act.contribution: Proposed action chunking: predicting a sequence of future actions with a single observation. Used a transformer with CVAE for diverse action generation. Enabled fine-grained bimanual manipulation on low-cost robots. Introduced temporal ensembling for smooth execution.

ablationStudy.finding: 100-step chunks provide good balance between coherence and reactivity
Reduces jitter and improves smoothness by 40%

bc.title: Behavior Cloning for Robotic Manipulation
bc.highlight: Classic supervised learning approach that directly imitates expert demonstrations. Foundation of modern VLA training pipelines.
bc.contribution: Formalized behavior cloning as supervised learning from expert trajectories. Introduced DAgger (Dataset Aggregation) to iteratively collect additional training data near the learned policy's state distribution. Foundation for modern VLA supervised pretraining.

ibc.title: Implicit Behavioral Cloning
ibc.highlight: Represents the policy as an energy-based model (EBM) that assigns high energy to expert actions and low energy to others, enabling multimodal action distributions.
ibc.contribution: Proposed representing policies as energy-based models using a critic network. Used contrastive learning to shape the energy landscape. Enabled multimodal behavior (choosing between multiple valid actions). Showed improved performance on tasks with multiple solution paths.

ablationStudy.finding: 16 negative samples sufficient; more does not help
Sharp energy minima correlate with precise action selection

rl-vla.title: RL Fine-Tuning for Vision-Language-Action Models
rl-vla.highlight: Survey reference on RL fine-tuning techniques for VLA models, including online RL, offline RL, and reward shaping.
rl-vla.contribution: Overview of RL fine-tuning for VLA: online RL (PPO, SAC) for task-specific optimization; offline RL (CQL, IQL) for conservative policy improvement; reward shaping using VLM-based reward models for open-ended tasks.

bridge.title: BridgeData: A Dataset for Learning Cross-Domain Robotic Manipulation
bridge.highlight: A diverse dataset of 7,200 teleoperated manipulation episodes across 71 tasks in 10 kitchen environments, designed for cross-domain generalization.
bridge.contribution: Collected 7,200 teleoperated episodes using a low-cost widowx robot. Covered 71 tasks in 10 diverse kitchen environments. Designed for cross-domain generalization with varying backgrounds, objects, and viewpoints. Became a core component of Open X-Embodiment.

openx.title: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models
openx.highlight: The largest open-source robot learning dataset, aggregating 1M+ trajectories from 22 robot embodiments across 60+ institutions worldwide.
openx.contribution: Aggregated 1M+ robot trajectories from 60+ institutions into a standardized format. Covered 22 robot embodiments and diverse task types. Trained RT-X (a 55B parameter VLA) on this dataset, demonstrating positive transfer across embodiments. Released standardized data pipeline and preprocessing tools.

droid.title: DROID: A Large-Scale In-The-Wild Robot Manipulation Dataset
droid.highlight: A diverse in-the-wild manipulation dataset with 76k trajectories collected across 564 scenes by 71 operators, capturing real-world variability.
droid.contribution: Collected 76k trajectories across 564 diverse scenes by 71 human operators. Captured real-world variability: lighting changes, clutter, distractors, different camera angles. Used for training generalist policies like Octo. Released with rich metadata and evaluation protocols.

calvin.title: CALVIN: A Benchmark for Language-Conditioned Policy Learning
calvin.highlight: A challenging benchmark for long-horizon language-conditioned manipulation with 34 tasks and a simulated Franka robot.
calvin.contribution: Introduced a benchmark with 34 long-horizon language-conditioned manipulation tasks. Uses a simulated Franka robot in a tabletop environment. Tasks require sequential reasoning (e.g., 'open drawer, take block, place in shelf'). Provides standardized evaluation protocol and leaderboard.

libero.title: LIBERO: Benchmarking Knowledge Transfer for Lifelong Robot Learning
libero.highlight: A benchmark for lifelong robot learning with 130 tasks across 10 task suites, evaluating knowledge transfer and continual learning.
libero.contribution: Introduced 130 manipulation tasks across 10 suites with varying difficulty. Evaluates knowledge transfer: learning new tasks while retaining old ones. Supports both simulation and real robot evaluation. Provides protocol for measuring catastrophic forgetting and forward transfer.
